title: From seed to flower to seed

steps.say: A flowering plant starts life as a seed. With water and warmth, the seed germinates and grows into a seedling.

figure.alt: The life cycle of a flowering plant: seed, seedling, adult plant, flower, and back to seed.

steps.say: The flower is where new seeds are made. Petals attract insects, and sepals protect the bud.
Anthers make pollen, and the stigma catches pollen. Moving pollen from an anther to a stigma is pollination.
Insects and the wind carry pollen. Bright, scented flowers attract insects, while dull flowers with light pollen use the wind.
When pollen joins with an ovule, that is fertilisation. The ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.
Seeds are spread by the wind, animals, water or bursting pods. Then the cycle starts again.

check.prompt: What does the stigma of a flower do?

options.why: The sepals protect the flower bud.

hints: The stigma is at the top of the carpel.
Think about what sticks to it when an insect visits.
check.explanation: The stigma is the sticky top of the carpel. It catches pollen during pollination.

check.prompt: Moving pollen from an anther to a stigma is called ___.
hints: Insects and the wind help it to happen.
The word starts with the same letters as pollen.
check.explanation: Pollination is the movement of pollen from an anther to a stigma.
